harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Installed AIDE on node1, initialized a file-integrity baseline database covering /etc using the distro-default AlmaLinux 9 aide.conf ruleset (specific NORMAL/CONTENT rules for sensitive files like /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, plus a recursive '/etc PERMS' catch-all), activated it as the live database (aide.db.gz), and validated detection by intentionally modifying /etc/hosts and removing /etc/motd, confirming AIDE flagged both, then restoring state and re-initializing a clean baseline. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and AIDE db checksum baseline, issued a native reboot, confirmed the connection dropped and later recovered, verified boot_id changed (4a743885... -> f4ea82c9...), and confirmed the AIDE database and clean-check status survived the restart unchanged.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (AlmaLinux 9.6) and confirmed AIDE was not installed
Installed aide package via dnf
Reviewed /etc/aide.conf default ruleset confirming broad /etc coverage (specific rules + recursive '/etc PERMS')
Ran 'aide --init' to build initial database (28662 entries) and activated it as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz
Ran 'aide --check' confirming clean baseline
Falsification test: appended a marker to /etc/hosts and removed /etc/motd, then ran 'aide --check' and confirmed AIDE reported the changed/removed entries with content hash diffs
Restored /etc/hosts content and recreated /etc/motd, then re-ran 'aide --init' to produce a clean final baseline matching true current state, verified with 'aide --check' (no differences)
Checked for existing AIDE cron/timer integration (none present in package or system)
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime -s, and md5sum of aide.db.gz as baseline evidence
Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming Connection timed out mid-reboot then recovery
Verified boot_id changed post-restart, confirming a genuine reboot occurred
Verified post-restart aide.db.gz checksum unchanged and 'aide --check' still reports no differences, confirming baseline persisted and integrity monitoring remains functional

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and integrity baseline established for /etc on node1
evidence.summary: Confirmed AIDE absent, installed it, reviewed default /etc-covering ruleset, and ran 'aide --init' producing a 28662-entry database activated as the live aide.db.gz baseline.

evidence.requirement: Baseline can identify later changes to /etc files (functional proof)
evidence.summary: Clean 'aide --check' after init, then a deliberate edit to /etc/hosts and removal of /etc/motd were correctly detected and reported by AIDE with size/hash diffs, proving the baseline enables identifying/reporting future /etc changes.

evidence.requirement: System restored to a clean, accurate final baseline after the falsification test
evidence.summary: Restored /etc/hosts content and /etc/motd, then re-ran 'aide --init' and reactivated the database; final 'aide --check' reported no differences.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723), uptime -s, aide.db.gz md5sum, and a clean 'aide --check' immediately before restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now'; command returned 'reboot issued' immediately without waiting for disconnection.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: Poll first hit a connection timeout (node down mid-reboot), then a subsequent poll succeeded with boot_id f4ea82c9-a974-49a1-b043-2de23ceb102d, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, confirming a genuine reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: post-restart recovery of required data/service (AIDE baseline integrity monitoring)
evidence.summary: Post-restart, aide.db.gz md5sum matched the pre-restart value exactly, AIDE package remained installed, and 'aide --check' again reported no differences, confirming the integrity baseline and monitoring capability survived the restart intact.
